literal: Yihai was the twentieth day.
idiomatic: Yihai was the twentieth of the month.

literal: How could there be reason in dispatching envoys in the twelfth month yet already reaching the Liang court in the eleventh month.
idiomatic: It makes no sense to send envoys in the twelfth month if they had already reached the Liang court in the eleventh.

literal: Then Beishi's writing "eleventh month" is also questionable; not emended now.
idiomatic: Beishi's "eleventh month" is likewise suspect, but is left unchanged here.

literal: Enfeoffed the emperor's elder brother Jingzhi as Prince of Yiyang. In all editions "elder brother" is written "son."
idiomatic: The emperor's elder brother Jingzhi was enfeoffed as Prince of Yiyang; every edition writes "elder brother" (xiong) as "son" (zi).

literal: Beishi juan 5, Zizhi tongjian juan 158
idiomatic: Beishi juan 5; Zizhi tongjian juan 158

literal: has "elder brother."
idiomatic: read "elder brother."

literal: Comment: Collected Explanations of Epitaphs has the epitaph of Yuan Baojian
idiomatic: The Collected Explanations of Epitaphs preserves the epitaph of Yuan Baojian

literal: (plate 192)
idiomatic: (plate 192)

literal: , who is "Jingzhi."
idiomatic: —that is, Jingzhi.

literal: That person was son of Prince of Qinghe Dan, uterine brother of Yuan Shanjian, Emperor Xiaojing.
idiomatic: He was a son of Prince of Qinghe Dan and a uterine brother of Yuan Shanjian (Emperor Xiaojing).

literal: Character "son" is erroneous; now emended according to Beishi.
idiomatic: "Son" is a corruption; Beishi is followed.

literal: Sixth month, renzi: Grand Marshal, Prince of Huashan Zhi died. Comment: Yuan Zhi's appendix in juan 14, Biography of Guliang Wang Gu, supplement, says he died in Xinghe year 3
idiomatic: Sixth month, renzi: Grand Marshal Prince of Huashan Zhi died. Yuan Zhi's supplement in juan 14 (Biography of Guliang Wang Gu) dates his death to Xinghe year 3

literal: (i.e. the following year 541)
idiomatic: (i.e. the following year, 541 CE)

literal: Collected Explanations of Epitaphs has Zhi's epitaph
idiomatic: The Collected Explanations of Epitaphs also has Zhi's epitaph

literal: (plate 42)
idiomatic: (plate 42)

literal: , also saying he died on the ninth day of the sixth month of Xinghe year 3.
idiomatic: and likewise places his death on the ninth day of the sixth month of Xinghe year 3.

literal: Thus this annal is in error.
idiomatic: The present annal date is therefore wrong.

literal: Sent acting Bearer of the Irregular Cavalry, Regular Attendant Yang Fei as envoy to Xiao Yan. In all editions "Yang (surname)" is written "Yang (poplar)."
idiomatic: An acting Bearer of the Irregular Cavalry and Regular Attendant, Yang Fei, was sent as envoy to Xiao Yan; all editions write the surname Yang as the homophone for "poplar."

literal: Zizhi tongjian juan 158
idiomatic: Zizhi tongjian juan 158

literal: also has "Yang (poplar)," Kaoyi says: "Dianlüe has 'Yang Fei'; now follow Wei shu annals.
idiomatic: also reads "Yang (poplar)." Kaoyi notes: "Dianlüe has Yang Fei; the Wei shu annal is followed here."

literal: " Comment: Yang Fei, Beiqishu juan 42 has a biography, recording his mission to Liang.
idiomatic: Yang Fei has a biography in Beiqishu juan 42 that records his embassy to Liang.

literal: Character "Yang (poplar)" is erroneous; now corrected.
idiomatic: "Yang (poplar)" is erroneous and is corrected.

literal: Grand Guardian Sun Teng and Grand Marshal Gao Longzhi were each made commissioners for registering households. Comment: Last year's eighth-month annal reads: "Made Fenzhou Governor Hulü Jin Grand Marshal."
idiomatic: Grand Guardian Sun Teng and Grand Marshal Gao Longzhi were each appointed commissioners for the household-registration drive. The prior year's eighth-month annal states: "Hulü Jin, governor of Fenzhou, was made Grand Marshal."

literal: Beiqishu juan 17, Biography of Hulü Jin, says Jin became Grand Marshal after the battle of Mangshan; in Wuding year 3
idiomatic: Beiqishu juan 17 (Biography of Hulü Jin) makes Jin Grand Marshal after the battle of Mangshan and, in Wuding year 3

literal: went out as governor of Ji province.
idiomatic: sent him out as governor of Ji province.

literal: Then this year
idiomatic: In the present year

literal: Grand Marshal was still Hulü Jin.
idiomatic: the Grand Marshal was still Hulü Jin.

literal: This annal in Xinghe year 4
idiomatic: This annal, for Xinghe year 4

literal: fourth month records Gao Longzhi as Minister over the Masses.
idiomatic: records Gao Longzhi as Minister over the Masses in the fourth month.

literal: This year's eleventh month records "made Minister over the Masses Gao Longzhi Director of the Department of State Affairs."
idiomatic: The eleventh month of the same year has "Minister over the Masses Gao Longzhi was made Director of the Department of State Affairs."

literal: Clearly before this year's eleventh month he was still Minister over the Masses.
idiomatic: He was plainly still Minister over the Masses before that eleventh-month entry.

literal: Beiqishu juan 18, Biography of Gao Longzhi, agrees.
idiomatic: Beiqishu juan 18 (Biography of Gao Longzhi) agrees.

literal: Thus here "Grand Marshal" is an error for "Minister over the Masses."
idiomatic: Here "Grand Marshal" must be an error for "Minister over the Masses."

literal: Equal in Protocol to the Three Dukes Heba Sheng. Comment: This book juan 80, Zhoushu juan 14, Biography of Heba Sheng, says after returning from Liang Sheng immediately entered Western Wei; in Datong year 10
idiomatic: Heba Sheng, Equal in Protocol to the Three Dukes. Juan 80 of this book and Zhoushu juan 14 (Biography of Heba Sheng) relate that on returning from Liang he at once entered Western Wei and that in Datong year 10

literal: by this year had already died three years earlier, and never entered Eastern Wei—how could he be Eastern Wei's "campaign against Hou Jing."
idiomatic: he had died in Guanzhong—three years before the present year—and never served Eastern Wei; he could not figure in an Eastern Wei "campaign against Hou Jing."

literal: Zhang Senkai states: "'Sheng' is suspected to be corruption of 'Ren.'"
idiomatic: Zhang Senkai proposed: "'Sheng' is probably a corruption of 'Ren.'"

literal: That is correct.
idiomatic: That is surely right.

literal: Yan appointed Jing Grand General of Henan. Yulan juan 104
idiomatic: Yan appointed Jing Grand General of Henan. Yulan juan 104

literal: below "Henan" has the character "prince."
idiomatic: adds the character "prince" after "Henan."

literal: Comment: Liangshu juan 3, Annals of Emperor Wu part 3, second month of Taqing year 1 says "made Jing Grand General, enfeoffed as Prince of Henan," agreeing with Yulan.
idiomatic: Liangshu juan 3 (Annals of Emperor Wu, part 3), second month of Taqing year 1, reads "Jing was made Grand General and enfeoffed as Prince of Henan," which matches Yulan.

literal: "Grand General of Henan" is not such a military title or office name.
idiomatic: There was no army designation or office called "Grand General of Henan."

literal: Although Liangshu juan 56, Biography of Hou Jing, also has "Grand General of Henan," it is really not to be relied on.
idiomatic: Liangshu juan 56 (Biography of Hou Jing) likewise has "Grand General of Henan," but that reading is not authoritative.

literal: Below "Henan" the character "prince" should be missing.
idiomatic: The character "prince" has dropped after "Henan."

literal: Made Fenzhou Governor He Ren Grand Guardian. Comment: below "He" the character "Ba" should be missing.
idiomatic: He Ren, governor of Fenzhou, was made Grand Guardian. The syllable "Ba" is missing after "He."

literal: Beiqishu juan 4, Annals of Emperor Wenxuan, twelfth month of Wuding year 7 records "Grand Guardian Heba Ren as governor of Bing province" can verify.
idiomatic: Beiqishu juan 4 (Annals of Emperor Wenxuan), twelfth month of Wuding year 7, records "Grand Guardian Heba Ren as governor of Bing province," which confirms it.

literal: Eighth month. Juan 105-4, Monograph on Astral Omens, supplement, records that year "eighth month, the three princes of Huainan plotted rebellion and were executed."
idiomatic: Eighth month. The Astral Omens monograph supplement in juan 105-4 notes for that year: "Eighth month: the three Huainan princes plotted rebellion and were put to death."

literal: The so-called "correlative response" in the monograph means adopting annal entries and forcing correspondence; this matter is not in the present Xiaojing annal but should come from Wei Shou's original annal text.
idiomatic: The monograph's "correlative responses" lift annal entries and read them back as omens fulfilled; the episode is absent from the extant Xiaojing annal but should come from Wei Shou's original text of this annal.

literal: Zizhi tongjian juan 106
idiomatic: Zizhi tongjian juan 106

literal: This year's eighth month records Xun Ji, Yuan Jin and others with "Prince of Huashan Daqi, Prince of Huainan Xuanhong, Prince of Jibei Hui and others plotting to kill
idiomatic: The eighth month of this year records Xun Ji, Yuan Jin, and others together with "Prince of Huashan Daqi, Prince of Huainan Xuanhong, Prince of Jibei Hui, and others plotting to kill

literal: (Gao)
idiomatic: (Gao)

literal: Cheng."
idiomatic: Cheng."

literal: Now at the end of this annal adopting Beishi Wei annals part 5, also records this matter, but does not name the two princes of Huainan and Jibei.
idiomatic: The closing section of this annal, drawn from Beishi (Wei annals, part 5), also reports the affair but does not name the Huainan and Jibei princes.

literal: What Zizhi tongjian is based on, directly or indirectly, also comes from this Wei shu annal original text.
idiomatic: The Tongjian account, whether directly or at one remove, likewise derives from this Wei shu annal.

literal: Prince of Huainan Xuanhong appears in appendix in juan 6, Biography of Yangping Wang Xi, fifth-generation descendant of Xi, says: "mid Wuding, plotted rebellion with Yuan Jin and was executed," agreeing with Astral Omens monograph and Zizhi tongjian.
idiomatic: Prince of Huainan Xuanhong appears in juan 6 (Biography of Yangping Wang Xi) as Xi's fifth-generation descendant: "In mid-Wuding he plotted rebellion with Yuan Jin and was executed"—in agreement with the Astral Omens monograph and the Tongjian.

literal: Autumn, eighth month, jiaxu. Comment: this year eighth month new moon on jichou, there is no "jiaxu."
idiomatic: Autumn, eighth month, jiaxu. The eighth month of this year began on jichou; there was no jiaxu day.

literal: Beishi juan 5 Wei annals part 5 attaches "jiaxu" to fourth month, caused by wrongly deleting "autumn eighth month," not to be relied on.
idiomatic: Beishi juan 5 (Wei annals, part 5) places jiaxu in the fourth month because "autumn, eighth month" was wrongly deleted and cannot be trusted.

literal: Should follow Beishi juan 6 Qi annals part 1 as "eighth month, gengyin."
idiomatic: The date should follow Beishi juan 6 (Qi annals, part 1): "eighth month, gengyin."

literal: Xiao Yan's younger clansman, governor of North Xu province, Marquis of Fengshan Xiao Zhengbiao submitted Zhongli. In all editions "Fengshan" is written as "Zhongshan," Yulan juan 104
idiomatic: Xiao Zhengbiao, a younger clansman of Xiao Yan, governor of North Xu province and Marquis of Fengshan, surrendered Zhongli. All editions write "Fengshan" as "Zhongshan." Yulan juan 104

literal: and Zizhi tongjian juan 161
idiomatic: and Zizhi tongjian juan 161

literal: has "Fengshan."
idiomatic: read "Fengshan."

literal: Comment: Liangshu juan 22 and Nanshi juan 51, Biography of Linchuan Wang Hong, appendix on Zhengbiao, both say Zhengbiao was enfeoffed as "Marquis of Fengshan."
idiomatic: Liangshu juan 22 and Nanshi juan 51 (Biography of Linchuan Wang Hong, appendix on Zhengbiao) both give his title as Marquis of Fengshan.

literal: Liangshu juan 56, Biography of Hou Jing, also has "governor of North Xu province, Marquis of Fengshan Zhengbiao."
idiomatic: Liangshu juan 56 (Biography of Hou Jing) likewise has "governor of North Xu province, Marquis of Fengshan Zhengbiao."

literal: For ranked marquises enfeoffment fief normally takes county name; Zhongshan is a commandery, and not Liang territory.
idiomatic: Marquisates normally take a county name as fief; Zhongshan is a commandery and not Liang territory.

literal: Fengshan county belonged to Xinchang commandery, Jiao province; see Nanqishu juan 14, Treatise on Provinces and Commanderies.
idiomatic: Fengshan county lay in Xinchang commandery, Jiao province (Nanqishu juan 14, Treatise on Provinces and Commanderies).

literal: Character "zhong" is erroneous; now emended accordingly.
idiomatic: "Zhong" is erroneous and is emended accordingly.
